newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo army recruits mutiny, cut rail link.
newsitem.headline: Congo army recruits mutiny, cut rail link.

text.p: Members of Congo's disbanded political militias, undergoing army training in the south west of the country, have launched an election year mutiny, cutting a key railway link to the sea, military sources said on Tuesday.

The mutineers, being trained at Loudima about 350 km (220 miles) south west of Brazzaville under a deal to end bloody ethnic and political rivalry, had set up barricades on the line between the capital and the economic capital of Pointe-Noire.
They launched the revolt on Saturday demanding immediate integration into the army with the rank of sergeant and seized control of Loudima station, they said.
A source close to the Chemin de Fer Congo Ocean (CFCO) rail company said no trains had travelled down the line since Saturday and that the mutineers were threatening to fire on any train that tried.
Further details were sketchy but the sources said a government and military neogotiating team had left for Loudima.
Congo is due to hold presidential elections in July. Already, President Pascal Lissouba, winner in 1992, has over half-a-dozen rivals jostling to take him on.

Fighting among militias loyal to Congo's political rivals after disputed legislative elections in 1993 killed an estimated 2,000 people in Brazzaville's suburbs. The militias officially disbanded in 1995 under a peace pact.

About 300 other militia fighters staged a similar revolt in Brazzaville in February 1996 and were integrated into the army. That revolt killed five people, three by stray bullet and two in an associated car crash.
